entry.title: 視聴という行為を「トレーニングの時間」に変える——Quest版YouTube刷新が示すVRの次の一手
entry.summary:
視聴という行為を「トレーニングの時間」に変える——Quest版YouTube刷新が示すVRの次の一手
GoogleがQuest向けYouTubeのイマーシブ表示を大幅に刷新しようとしている——UploadVRが報じたこの動きは、VRヘッドセットが「動画を見るためだけのデバイス」から「毎日使う実用的なツール」へと変わりつつあることを示しています。 エンジニアの視点で面白いのは、これが単なるUIの刷新ではなく、レンダリングパイプラインと知覚の設計問題だという点です。イマーシブ表示では、動画は平面テクスチャとして頭部トラッキング空間にマッピングされ、フレームごとにステレオ再投影が走ります。ここで問われるのは「どれだけ没入できるか」ではなく、「その没入を何に転用できるか」です。受動的な消費の時間を、意図的なトレーニングの時間へ——この転用可能性こそが、プラットフォーム成熟の本当の指標だと私は考えています。 弱視（amblyopia）やlazy eye（怠惰眼）を持つ人にとって、従来の視覚トレーニングは道具（遮蔽用パッチ、赤青メガネ）と単調な反復が前提でした。継続のハードルは、効果以前に「面白くない」ことでした。つまりこれは、臨床というよりエンゲージメント設計の問題です。 AmblyotubeはSeven Sportsが開発したMeta Quest向けのリクリエーション＆教育ソフトウェアです。左右の目に異なる視覚体験を提示し、YouTube形式のコンテンツをそのまま視覚トレーニングの場に変えます。 アーキテクチャとして興味深いのは、眼ごとにシェーダーを分岐させている点です。 ・利き目側には調整可能なデジタルブラー（Dominant Eye Shader）——抑制側の信号を意図的に劣化させる パラメータを眼ごとに独立制御できる設計は、単一シェーダーで全体をぼかす素朴な実装より調整自由度が高く、結果として「毎日続けられる負荷」に着地しやすくなります。推奨は1日30〜40分（最大1時間）、13歳以上。補助的な視覚トレーニング／支援ツールであり、診断・治療・治癒を目的としたものではありません。 コンテンツが面白ければ、続く。VRプラットフォームの成熟は、視覚トレーニングの継続率という古い課題に、現実的な答えを一つ増やします。 Meta Questアプリ：https://www.meta.com/en-gb/experiences/amblyotube/25906906972338493/

entry.title: How to Stop Clients Paying Your Freelance Dev Invoices Late
entry.summary:
Late payment is one of the most common freelance problems. Remote's 2025 contractor report found that 85% of freelancers are paid late at least some of the time. Bonsai's analysis of invoice data from over 100,000 freelancers found that 29% of invoices were paid at least a day late. Most of the time, the client isn't trying to cheat you. The invoice got lost, stuck in approval, or rejected for a missing PO number. A late invoice is usually a process problem, so you fix it with a process. Check the client before you quote Red flags to watch for: No written scope or agreement Split the work into milestones Don't bill one big invoice at the end. For example: 30% to start Put three clauses in your contract
Send a reminder before the due date
Hi [Name], a quick note that invoice [#] for [amount] is due on [date]. The payment link is here: [link]. If it's with finance already, thank you. If anything is holding it up, tell me and I'll sort it. Follow a fixed sequence when it's overdue A script removes the emotion: Day 1: friendly reminder asking when to expect payment. Don't hand over everything before you're paid Release final files, repo transfer and production credentials only after the final invoice is paid. Put that in the contract first, not at the end of the project. Free scripts https://whop.com/checkout/plan_YyJkQdzaErxZw This is general information, not legal advice. Laws on late payment vary by country and state.

entry.title: Kamau Therapeutics just shared compelling preclinical data ahead of ASH: precise correc...
entry.summary:
Kamau Therapeutics just shared compelling preclinical data ahead of ASH: precise correc...
When Gene Editing Hits the Clinic, We Need Better Ways to See the Edit: A Builder's Personal Walk Through β-Globin in VR I stood in the cold‑room of the genomics core at 2 a.m., the sequencer humming like a tired server. My CRISPR‑Cas9 construct targeting the β‑globin locus had just returned a clean on‑target read, but the off‑target report was a spreadsheet of coordinates that meant nothing until I could walk them. The VR viewer we built — a Unity‑based point‑cloud engine that streams variant calls from a GraphQL endpoint — let me drop into a 3‑D nucleus, scale the chromatin to meter‑size, and watch the edit glow in real time. Frame‑rate held at 92 fps on a single RTX 3080, latency under 12 ms, enough to rotate the model without nausea. The first time I turned the helix, I saw a silent insertion three kilobases downstream that the flat heatmap had missed. My heart jumped; the patient’s genotype was clean, but the model warned me. I rewrote the guide, re‑ran the simulation, and the offending signal vanished. That night I shipped the corrected construct to the GMP facility, and the downstream assay came back clean. Seeing the genome as a space you can inhabit changes the feedback loop from “run‑analyze‑wait” to “run‑see‑decide.” If you’re wrestling with therapeutic editing, try stepping inside the data. The next iteration of the viewer adds collaborative annotations and a Python SDK for batch validation — come walk the helix with me. I still hear the sequencer’s whir when I close my eyes, and each new dataset feels like a fresh room to explore. If you’re building the next generation of gene‑therapy tools, the viewer’s open API lets you plug in your own QC metrics — join the repo, file an issue, and let’s make the invisible visible together.

entry.title: Debugging 429 Bursts and Retry-After
entry.summary: Quick answer: When 429 responses arrive in a burst, the first thing to check is the client's retry behavior, not the server's limit. A burst usually means callers are retrying at the same instant and amplifying the load. Read the Retry-After header, wait that long before the next attempt, and use exponential backoff with jitter so retries spread out instead of landing together. A single 429 means one request crossed a rate or quota window. A burst means many callers hit the limit together, or one caller's retries are generating fresh traffic faster than the window can recover. The two feel identical from the client, but they have different fixes. Raising the server limit only helps if genuine demand exceeds it; if the burst is a retry storm, a higher limit just delays the next failure. The…
